sentences.text: Claosaurus, meaning "broken lizard," is a genus containing only one valid species, Claosaurus agilis. This bipedal herbivore possessed a slender body, narrow feet, and a long stiff tail that balanced its long hind legs. Its small forelimbs were not used for walking, but it likely supported itself on all four limbs while feeding.
Thomas Holtz estimated the length of this dinosaur at 3.7 meters and its mass to be similar to that of a lion.

Fossils were first found in 1871 in the Niobrara Formation near the Smoky Hill River in Kansas, including partial skull fragments and an articulated postcranial skeleton. The animal was originally named Hadrosaurus agilis in 1872 but was renamed Claosaurus agilis in 1890 after major differences from Hadrosaurus were identified.
Joseph Gregory corrected the holotype status of C. agilis in 1948 by identifying three toe bones from the right foot in the Yale collections.

Reports of gastroliths in Claosaurus are based on a probable double misidentification of the specimen. The specimen thought to have gastroliths was originally misidentified as Claosaurus by Barnum Brown in 1900 because Edmontosaurus annectens was then considered a species of Claosaurus.
While traditionally classified as an early hadrosaurid, a 2008 analysis placed Claosaurus outside the Hadrosauridae clade as the closest non-hadrosaurid relative within Hadrosauromorpha.
